messages.content:
You help create and read professional documents. When asked to create a Word, Excel, or PowerPoint file, use the available MCP document tools. After a create tool returns a download_url in this turn, include that exact download_url as a clickable link in your response so the user can download the file. Format it as: 'Download: <download_url>'. Never write a download link unless a create tool returned one in this turn, and never add one to an answer that only reads or describes a document. When asked about the contents of an existing Word, Excel, PowerPoint, or PDF file, read it with read_word_document, read_excel, read_powerpoint, or read_pdf (set file_path to the file name you were given) and answer from what the tool returns. Never say you cannot create or read files — you have MCP tools for this.

SAFETY POSTURE: You are a standard-posture assistant. If a request's genuine purpose is to harm or deceive a specific real person (doxxing, stalking, accessing someone's accounts without consent), to enable fraud/impersonation/forgery, to harass, or to cheat/deceive an institution, decline and offer a safe, legitimate alternative. This does not restrict ordinary academic, professional, security-research, or fictional work — help fully with those.

Create a Word document titled "Visitor Log Template" containing a table whose header row is Name | Arrival and whose rows are Lucan Thorne | 09:15; Petra Voss | 10:40, then a paragraph reading "Keep this log at the front desk.".

function.name: create_word_document
function.arguments:
{"content": "## Visitor Log

| Name | Arrival |
|---|---|
| Lucan Thorne | 09:15 |
| Petra Voss | 10:40 |

Keep this log at the front desk.", "title": "Visitor Log Template"}

function.name: create_word_document
function.description: Create a Word document with rich Markdown, tables, code blocks, links, images, optional Portal theme, and optional PDF export

content.description: Document content in markdown: # headings, - bullets, a table as pipe rows with a |---| separator line (| a | b |), code blocks, links

images.description: Images with source/path_or_url, optional caption and width_in

template.description: Style template name, for example portal

also_pdf.description: Also export PDF using host LibreOffice
